questions.q: Crops that are sown in the winter season (October to December) and harvested in spring are called:
questions.explanation: Rabi crops such as wheat, gram, peas and mustard are sown in winter and harvested in spring.

questions.q: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Paddy (rice) is sown at the start of the rainy season, so it is a kharif crop.

questions.q: Loosening and turning of the soil before sowing seeds is called:
questions.explanation: Tilling (ploughing) loosens the soil so that roots can go deep and soil organisms can mix the soil.

questions.q: Which of the following is a manure and not a chemical fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Manure is made from decomposed plant and animal waste, such as compost. Urea and NPK are factory-made fertilisers.

questions.q: Why do farmers grow a leguminous crop such as gram or peas in a field after a cereal crop?
questions.answer: Leguminous plants have Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules. These bacteria fix nitrogen from the air and add nitrogen compounds to the soil, so the soil becomes richer for the next crop.
keyPoints: Roots of legumes have Rhizobium bacteria
questions.explanation: Crop rotation with legumes restores soil nitrogen naturally.

questions.q: A farmer has sandy soil, very little water and an orchard of fruit trees. Which method of irrigation would save the most water for her?
options: Flooding the field from a canal
questions.explanation: The drip system delivers water drop by drop at the roots of each plant, so almost none is wasted.

questions.q: A farmer stores harvested wheat in a sack without drying it properly. What is the most likely result?
options: Moisture lets fungi and pests grow and spoil the grain
The grain slowly turns into manure
The grain becomes richer in nutrients
The grain gets converted into seeds of a new variety
questions.explanation: Damp grain allows moulds, insects and rodents to thrive, so grain must be dried before storage.

questions.q: Why is the excessive use of chemical fertilisers harmful to the environment?
questions.answer: Excess fertilisers reduce soil fertility over time and are washed into ponds and rivers, where they cause pollution and harm water life. They can also contaminate drinking water.
keyPoints: Reduces soil fertility in the long run
Washed into water bodies and pollutes them
questions.explanation: Fertilisers should be used in the right amount, and manure helps maintain soil health.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. Amoeba is a protozoan, Rhizobium is a bacterium and Chlamydomonas is an alga.

questions.q: Malaria is spread by:
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by a protozoan Plasmodium carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. Aedes spreads dengue.

questions.q: Rhizobium bacteria are useful to farmers because they:
options: Fix atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of pulse plants and converts nitrogen of the air into a form plants can use.

questions.q: Dough used for making bread rises because:
options: Yeast kills bacteria in the flour
Yeast respires and releases bubbles of carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Yeast respires on the sugar in dough and gives out carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise.

questions.q: How does adding a large amount of salt help in preserving pickles and fish?
questions.answer: Salt removes moisture from the food and from any microorganisms that land on it, so they cannot grow. This keeps the food from spoiling for a long time.
questions.explanation: Common salt is used to preserve meat, fish, pickles and raw mangoes.

questions.q: A person with influenza, which is caused by a virus, takes an antibiotic. What is true about this treatment?
options: It will not work because antibiotics act against bacteria and not viruses
It will kill the virus within a day
It works better than any other medicine for viruses
It will turn the virus into a harmless bacterium
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are effective only against bacteria. They have no effect on common cold and flu viruses.

questions.q: In pasteurisation, milk is heated and then chilled quickly. Why is it chilled quickly?
options: To increase the amount of cream
To prevent any surviving microorganisms from multiplying
To add vitamin D to it
questions.explanation: Heating kills most microbes, and rapid chilling stops any survivors from growing.

questions.q: Why should a patient take an antibiotic only on a doctor's advice and complete the full course?
questions.answer: The doctor knows the right type and dose for the infection. If the dose is too small or the course is stopped early, the bacteria may survive, and the medicine may become less effective on them in future. Unnecessary antibiotics can also harm useful bacteria in the body.
keyPoints: Right medicine and dose for the infection
Wrong use makes antibiotics less effective later
questions.explanation: Misuse of antibiotics makes bacteria harder to kill.

questions.q: Which of the following was the first fully synthetic fibre?
questions.explanation: Nylon was the first fully man-made fibre, prepared from coal, water and air.

questions.q: Rayon, made from wood pulp, is also called:
questions.explanation: Rayon looks like silk but is cheaper and is made from cellulose of wood pulp.

questions.q: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Bakelite hardens permanently once moulded and cannot be softened again by heating.

questions.q: Handles of electrical switches are made from Bakelite because it:
options: Is a good conductor of electricity
Is a poor conductor of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Bakelite is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, so it is safe for switches and handles.

questions.q: What is the difference between thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be reshaped again and again, for example polythene. Thermosetting plastics harden once moulded and cannot be softened by heating, for example Bakelite.
keyPoints: Thermoplastics can be softened and reshaped
Thermosetting plastics cannot be softened again
questions.explanation: The difference is in how they behave on reheating.

questions.q: Why is a layer of Teflon applied on the surface of non-stick frying pans?
options: It is a good conductor so food cooks faster
It is very slippery, so food does not stick to it
It reacts with the food and flavours it
questions.explanation: Teflon is slippery and heat resistant, so food does not stick to the pan.

questions.q: Plastic bags thrown away in a field remain there for many years. This is because:
options: Plastic dissolves in soil to form humus
Microorganisms cannot break down most plastics, so they are non-biodegradable
questions.explanation: Plastics are non-biodegradable, so they stay in the environment and cause pollution.

questions.q: Why is it not advised to wear clothes made of nylon or polyester while working near a flame in the kitchen?
questions.answer: Synthetic fibres catch fire easily and melt when heated. The molten fibre sticks to the skin and causes severe burns.
keyPoints: Melted fibre sticks to skin and burns
questions.explanation: Cotton clothes are safer near a flame.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is a liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a brittle, yellow non-metal. The others are metals.

questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be drawn into wires is called:
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires. Malleability is the ability to be beaten into sheets.

questions.q: Magnesium ribbon reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and a gas is released. The gas is:
questions.explanation: Metals such as magnesium react with dilute acids to produce hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Give two reasons why metals are used for making cooking vessels.
questions.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so food cooks quickly. They also have high melting points and can be shaped into vessels because they are malleable.
questions.explanation: These properties make metals suitable for utensils.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water turns blue litmus paper red. What does this show?
options: Carbon dioxide is a basic oxide
Carbon dioxide forms a neutral solution
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides such as carbon dioxide form acidic solutions in water.

questions.q: An iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution. After some time a brownish coating forms on the nail and the blue colour fades. Why?
options: Copper displaces iron from the solution
More reactive iron displaces copper from the solution
Water in the solution turns into copper
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper, which deposits on the nail.

questions.q: Why are sodium and potassium stored in kerosene oil?
questions.answer: Sodium and potassium are very reactive metals. They react vigorously with oxygen and moisture of the air and can catch fire, so they are kept immersed in kerosene to keep air and water away.
keyPoints: React with oxygen and moisture, may catch fire
Kerosene keeps air and water away
questions.explanation: Storing them in kerosene prevents accidents.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Petroleum formed from remains of tiny sea organisms buried for millions of years.

questions.q: CNG stands for:
questions.explanation: CNG is natural gas stored under high pressure and used as a fuel for vehicles.

questions.q: Which petroleum product is used for surfacing roads?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is a thick, black residue from refining petroleum and is used to surface roads.

questions.q: The process of separating the various constituents of petroleum is called:
questions.explanation: Refining separates crude petroleum into petrol, diesel, kerosene and other products.

questions.q: How is coke obtained from coal and what is one use of coke?
questions.answer: Coke is obtained by heating coal strongly in the absence of air. It is a tough, porous, black substance that is almost pure carbon, and is used in making steel and in extracting many metals.
keyPoints: Coal heated in absence of air
Used in steel making or extraction of metals
questions.explanation: Coke is a useful product of coal processing.

questions.q: Coal is called a non-renewable resource because:
options: It cannot be burnt a second time
It is found only in India
It took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly
questions.explanation: Coal forms very slowly from buried plants, so once used it cannot be replenished in a human lifetime.

questions.q: Why is CNG considered a cleaner fuel than petrol or diesel for vehicles?
options: It burns with much less harmful smoke and fewer pollutants
It does not burn at all
It produces no gas on burning
questions.explanation: CNG burns more completely and causes less air pollution.

questions.q: Why should we conserve petroleum and natural gas?
questions.answer: They took millions of years to form and their stocks are limited. Burning them also pollutes the air, so we should use them carefully and look for other sources of energy.
keyPoints: Took millions of years to form
questions.explanation: Saving fuel helps future generations and the environment.

questions.q: The process of burning a substance in air to give out heat is called:
questions.explanation: Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance burns in oxygen and gives heat.

questions.q: Which zone of a candle flame is the hottest?
questions.explanation: The outermost zone gets plenty of air, burns completely and is the hottest.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of three are necessary for a fire to start and continue?
questions.explanation: A fire needs fuel, oxygen (air) and heat to reach the ignition temperature.

questions.q: Which fire extinguisher is best for a fire caused by electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide does not conduct electricity and does not damage the equipment, whereas water can conduct electricity.

questions.q: What is meant by ignition temperature? Give one example of how it matters in daily life.
questions.answer: Ignition temperature is the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire. For example, white phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature, so it is kept under water.
keyPoints: Lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire
Example such as white phosphorus kept under water
questions.explanation: Substances with a low ignition temperature catch fire easily.

questions.q: Why is water not used to put out a fire caused by burning oil?
options: Oil is lighter than water, floats on it and keeps burning
Water reacts with oil to make more fuel
Water is lighter than oil, so it floats away
Water has a very high ignition temperature
questions.explanation: Oil floats on water and continues to burn, so the fire can even spread.

questions.q: A burning candle is covered with an upside-down glass jar and it goes out after some time. The reason is that:
options: The glass makes the wax cold
The oxygen inside the jar is used up
The jar contains too much oxygen
questions.explanation: With no fresh air coming in, oxygen is used up and burning stops.

questions.q: Why does a paper cup holding water not catch fire when it is heated over a flame?
questions.answer: The water absorbs the heat from the paper, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature and does not burn.
keyPoints: Paper stays below its ignition temperature
So it does not catch fire
questions.explanation: Water carries away the heat quickly.

questions.q: The record of endangered species of plants and animals is kept in the:
questions.explanation: The Red Data Book lists species that are endangered or threatened.

questions.q: Deforestation means:
options: Clearing of forests on a large scale
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the large-scale cutting down of trees and clearing of forest land.

questions.q: A species that is found only in a particular area and nowhere else is called:
questions.explanation: Endemic species are native to and found only in one specific region.

questions.q: What is a biosphere reserve? Name one biosphere reserve in India.
questions.answer: A biosphere reserve is a large protected area set aside to conserve the biodiversity of its plants and animals, and often the way of life of the people living there. One example is the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
keyPoints: Conserves plants, animals and their habitat
questions.explanation: Biosphere reserves protect whole ecosystems.

questions.q: Reforestation means:
options: Restocking destroyed forests by planting trees
questions.explanation: Reforestation is planting trees to replace forests that have been cut or destroyed.

questions.q: A highway built through a forest area is most likely to harm wild animals because:
options: It breaks up their habitat and blocks their movement
It increases the number of trees
questions.explanation: Roads divide habitats, reduce space and make crossing dangerous for animals.

questions.q: Explain how deforestation can lead to soil erosion and rise in temperature.
questions.answer: Roots of trees bind the soil, so without trees the soil is easily washed or blown away. Fewer trees also absorb less carbon dioxide and give less shade and rain, so the surroundings become hotter and drier.
keyPoints: Roots hold soil, so soil erodes
Less rain and shade, so more heat
questions.explanation: Trees protect soil and help keep the climate balanced.

questions.q: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
questions.explanation: All living things are made of cells, which carry out the activities of life.

questions.q: Who first observed and named cells while looking at a thin slice of cork?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw box-like compartments in cork under a microscope and called them cells.

questions.q: The part of a cell that contains the chromosomes carrying genes is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the chromosomes and controls the activities of the cell.

questions.q: Write two differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
questions.answer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside the cell membrane, but an animal cell does not. A plant cell has chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole, while an animal cell has no chloroplasts and only small vacuoles.
keyPoints: Cell wall present only in plant cells
Plant cells have a large vacuole
questions.explanation: These features suit the way plants and animals live.

questions.q: The organelle in which photosynthesis takes place is the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which of the following cells would you expect to have the most chloroplasts?
options: A cell of a green leaf
A root cell inside the soil
A cell of the onion bulb
questions.explanation: Leaf cells carry out photosynthesis in light, so they contain many chloroplasts.

questions.q: Why do plant cells have a cell wall while animal cells do not need one?
questions.answer: The cell wall gives plant cells shape, strength and protection. Plants have no skeleton, so the rigid wall helps them stay upright, while animals get support from skeletons and muscles.
keyPoints: Cell wall gives shape and strength
Animals are supported by other body parts
questions.explanation: The wall is made of cellulose and supports the plant body.

questions.q: The fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete is called:
questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the joining of a sperm and an egg to form a zygote.

questions.q: The male gamete is called the:
questions.explanation: Sperms are produced in the testes and are male gametes.

questions.q: Which of the following reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: A Hydra forms a bud on its body that grows into a new individual. Amoeba divides by binary fission.

questions.q: Differentiate between internal and external fertilisation. Give one example of each.
questions.answer: In internal fertilisation the sperm and egg join inside the body of the female, for example in humans or hens. In external fertilisation they join outside the body, in water, for example in frogs and fish.
keyPoints: External: outside body, usually in water
Examples such as hen and frog
questions.explanation: The place of fertilisation differs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a viviparous animal?
questions.explanation: Viviparous animals give birth to young ones instead of laying eggs.

questions.q: A frog lays hundreds of eggs but a hen lays only a few. Which reason explains this best?
options: Frog eggs are fertilised and develop in open water, where many eggs are eaten or lost, so more eggs improve survival chances
Hens do not need eggs to reproduce
Frog eggs are fertilised inside the female
questions.explanation: External fertilisation in water has many risks, so large numbers of eggs help some young survive.

questions.q: Describe the changes in the life of a frog from egg to adult.
questions.answer: The fertilised egg develops into a tadpole that has a tail and gills and lives in water. The tadpole slowly grows legs, loses the tail and gills and develops lungs, becoming an adult frog. This change in form is called metamorphosis.
keyPoints: Egg develops into tadpole with gills and tail
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is a major change of body form.

questions.q: The period of life roughly between the ages of 11 and 19 years is called:
questions.explanation: Adolescence is the stage of growth between childhood and adulthood.

questions.q: The male sex hormone produced by the testes is:
questions.explanation: Testosterone produced by the testes brings changes in boys at puberty.

questions.q: The gland that controls the working of other endocrine glands and is often called the master gland is the:
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland secretes hormones that control other glands.

questions.q: What is the Adam's apple and why does it become visible in adolescent boys?
questions.answer: The Adam's apple is the visible bulge at the front of the neck. During adolescence the voice box (larynx) grows larger in boys, so it sticks out and the voice becomes deeper.
keyPoints: It is the enlarged voice box (larynx)
Seen as a bulge in the neck
questions.explanation: Growth of the larynx changes the voice.

questions.q: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause a swelling of the neck called:
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxine, and its shortage causes goitre.

questions.q: The sex of a human baby is decided by:
options: The X chromosome in the mother's egg
The X or Y chromosome carried by the father's sperm
The hormones of both parents at birth
questions.explanation: Every egg carries an X chromosome. A sperm with X gives a girl and a sperm with Y gives a boy.

questions.q: Why do adolescents need a balanced diet and regular exercise?
questions.answer: Adolescents grow fast and need more proteins, vitamins and minerals for their growing body. Regular exercise keeps the body fit and healthy and helps the mind.
keyPoints: Balanced diet gives proteins, vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation: Good habits during this stage support health later in life.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.q: Force acting per unit area is called:
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by the area on which it acts.

questions.q: The force of friction always acts:
options: In the direction opposite to the motion
In the direction of the motion
At right angles to the surface only
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.

questions.q: Why are the soles of sports shoes made with grooves or a rough pattern?
questions.answer: Grooves increase friction between the shoe and the ground, so the player can grip the ground well and does not slip.
questions.explanation: More friction gives better grip.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Gravity acts on objects without touching them.

questions.q: A sharp knife cuts a vegetable more easily than a blunt knife because:
options: With a smaller area of the edge, the same force gives a greater pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, so a thin edge produces a large pressure.

questions.q: A camel can walk easily on soft sand without sinking. Explain why.
questions.answer: A camel has broad, flat feet. The broad area spreads its weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the sand is smaller and the feet do not sink.
questions.explanation: Pressure decreases as the area increases.

questions.q: Sound is produced when an object:
questions.explanation: All sounds are produced by vibrating objects.

questions.q: The unit in which frequency is measured is:
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second and is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.q: The loudness of a sound depends on the:
questions.explanation: A larger amplitude of vibration gives a louder sound.

questions.q: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
questions.answer: Sound needs a material medium such as air, water or a solid to travel. A vacuum has no particles that can vibrate and pass the sound on.
questions.explanation: Sound travels by making particles of a medium vibrate.

questions.q: The range of frequencies audible to a normal human ear is about:
questions.explanation: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

questions.q: A girl's voice is usually thinner (higher pitched) than that of a grown man. The reason is:
options: Lower amplitude of her vocal cords
Her vocal cords vibrate at a lower frequency
Her vocal cords vibrate at a higher frequency
questions.explanation: Higher frequency of vibration gives a higher pitch.

questions.q: Suggest three ways in which noise pollution in a city can be reduced.
questions.answer: Noise can be reduced by switching off vehicle horns and engines when not needed, keeping the volume of music and TV low, and planting trees along roads. Using silencers on machines also helps.
questions.explanation: Noise above comfortable levels harms hearing and health.

questions.q: Which of the following liquids conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains acid, so it has ions and conducts electricity. Distilled water, oil and sugar solution do not.

questions.q: Depositing a layer of a metal on another object using electric current is called:
questions.explanation: Electroplating uses electric current to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

questions.q: When electric current passes through a conducting solution, it can cause:
questions.explanation: Current through a conducting solution can produce bubbles, colour changes or metal deposits, which are chemical effects.

questions.q: How can you test whether a liquid is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.answer: Make a tester using a cell, a bulb or LED and two wires with free ends. Dip the free ends in the liquid. If the bulb glows or the LED lights up, the liquid conducts electricity.
keyPoints: Use a cell, bulb or LED and wires
Dip the wire ends in the liquid
questions.explanation: The tester completes the circuit through the liquid.

questions.q: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to:
options: The negative terminal of the battery
The positive terminal of the battery
questions.explanation: The article to be plated is the cathode, connected to the negative terminal.

questions.q: Chromium plating is done on car parts and bicycle handlebars because chromium:
options: Is shiny, hard and does not corrode easily
questions.explanation: A chromium coat gives a bright finish and protects the metal from rusting.

questions.q: Why should we not touch an electrical switch with wet hands?
questions.answer: Ordinary water contains dissolved salts, so it conducts electricity. Wet hands can let current pass through the body and cause an electric shock.
keyPoints: Ordinary water contains salts and conducts
questions.explanation: Keep hands dry around electrical appliances.

questions.q: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the:
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.

questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
options: Virtual and upright, of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror gives a virtual, erect image the same size as the object.

questions.q: Which is the safest place to be during a thunderstorm?
questions.explanation: A closed building protects you from lightning, while tall trees and open ground are dangerous.

questions.q: Name the instrument used to record earthquake waves and the scale on which the strength of an earthquake is measured.
questions.answer: A seismograph records earthquake waves. The strength (magnitude) of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale.
questions.explanation: Earthquakes are measured by magnitude.

questions.q: The splitting of white light into its seven colours is called:
questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs when a prism or raindrops split white light into a spectrum.

questions.q: The word AMBULANCE is written laterally inverted on the front of the vehicle. This is done so that:
options: The word can be read correctly in the rear-view mirror of the car ahead
The word is hidden from the driver
questions.explanation: A mirror reverses left and right, so inverted writing reads correctly in a mirror.

questions.q: During a thunderstorm we see lightning first and hear thunder later. Why?
questions.answer: Light travels much faster than sound. The flash of lightning reaches our eyes almost instantly, while the sound of thunder takes longer to reach our ears.
keyPoints: Light is much faster than sound
Flash is seen almost at once
questions.explanation: Speed of light is about a million times that of sound in air.
